svg.title: A wooden prairie grain elevator beside the track, drawn from the surviving Pioneer elevator at Chamberlain, Saskatchewan: a tall gable-roofed crib in red-oxide painted timber with ochre gable and eaves trim, a cupola straddling the ridge, a driveway annex with a shed roof and a through opening a truck drives into, an office lean-to, a loading spout to the track side, and a siding rail in the apron. PROPORTIONS MEASURED TWICE AND THEY AGREE: on assets/refs/prairie-rail/grain-elevator-chamberlain.jpg the crib is 380 px wide and 870 px to the apex, and on grain-elevator-sintaluta-elevation.jpg the same figures are 270 and 615 - HEIGHT : WIDTH 2.29 and 2.28. Gable rise 0.30 of the crib width (0.25 and 0.35 on the two references, and this is their mean, recorded as a mean rather than left looking like a measurement). Cupola 0.30 of the crib width across and rising 0.44 of it above the apex, measured on the Sintaluta elevation, which is the near-orthographic one. Annex 1.45 crib widths long against Chamberlain's apparent 1.68: that photograph is taken close and low and the annex recedes hard away from the camera, so its apparent length is a projection and is NOT used. THE GABLE END AND THE ANNEX FLANK ARE BOTH DRAWN FRONTAL, which is what assets/refs/prairie-rail/grain-elevator-govan-and-track.jpg shows from beside the line and is how an elevator reads from a train. NO LETTERING: the company name and the town name are painted across every elevator in every reference and this project draws none, so this one ships blank - which is why its blind contract asks for a grain elevator and never for a place.
